project: A municipal sports complex: bookings with setup and teardown buffers that may never overlap.

steps.title: The complex, as a day you can look at
steps.scene: Four grounds, opening hours that differ on Sundays, and six event types each with its own setup and teardown. All of it lives on a wall planner, in pencil.
steps.build: Load grounds, hours, event types and their buffers once at start-up from a settings object, and serve a day that can be read as blocks and the shadows around them — the shadow derived from the event type, never stored as a second booking somebody has to remember to move.
steps.follows: Nothing can be requested, confirmed or moved until the complex exists.

story.want: see a ground's day as blocks and the setup and teardown around them
story.so: I can see the real shape of the day, not just the matches

steps.summary: The app starts with four grounds, their opening hours and six event types with buffers loaded once, and answers a day as blocks with the shadows around them.

event_types(id, venue_id, code, name, setup_minutes, teardown_minutes)
seed files seed/grounds.csv, seed/event_types.csv read once at start-up
rules: The shadow is computed on read from the booking's event type: `ground_held_from = from − setup`, `ground_held_to = to + teardown`. No column stores it.
Seeding is idempotent.
Settings (database path, host, port) from one settings object.
Opening hours depend on the weekday: Sunday uses the sunday_* columns.
Filters are typed query parameters bound to enums; every response goes through a declared response model (no bare dicts).

steps.title: A club asks for a slot
steps.scene: Rafi calls Deepa for Saturday, two till five. He does not say that his ground staff arrive at twenty past one, because on the planner that has never mattered.
steps.build: A request endpoint taking an interval and an event type through a request model with real constraints, answering 201 — and separating a malformed interval (422) from one that ends before it starts or falls outside the ground's hours (400).
steps.follows: The day is readable; this is the first thing that changes it, so validation lives here.

story.want: request a slot by interval and event type
story.so: my booking carries the setup time my ground staff actually need

steps.summary: A club requests a slot by ground, interval and event type and gets a `requested` booking back; an impossible interval is refused differently from a malformed body.

codes: the body fails validation; `errors[]` names each field
`to` is not after `from`, or the interval crosses the ground's opening hours; `opens`/`closes` say the hours
no such ground at this venue
no such booking at this venue

data: bookings(id, venue_id, ground_id, event_type_id, club_name, from_at, to_at, state requested|confirmed|cancelled|expired, requested_at, hold_until); settings HOLD_HOURS (24)
rules: `from` and `to` must parse, `to` > `from`, `from` not before the injected clock's now (nobody books the past), both on the same date, and the *shadow* must lie within the ground's hours for that weekday — everything after parsing is 400 bad-interval (valid body, impossible request).
Minimum interval 30 minutes, maximum 12 hours — validation.
`hold_until` = requested_at + HOLD_HOURS from the injected clock. No overlap check yet.
The request model uses `Field` constraints; a body that fails them is 422, a body that passes but asks for something impossible is 400 — two different types, tested separately.

The red panel: 17:00-14:00 is 400 bad-interval; 06:20-08:00 is 400 bad-interval naming `opens` 06:00 because the shadow would start at 05:40; a missing `from` is 422 validation naming the field — a valid body that asks the impossible is a different type from a malformed one.

steps.title: Confirm, cancel, and the hour that has already gone
steps.scene: A club cancels a slot that started twenty minutes ago and expects it back on the planner as free. The same afternoon, Sabu tries to confirm a slot that has already begun.
steps.build: Confirm and cancel as real transitions, with the rules that depend on the current time — you cannot confirm a slot that has begun, you cannot cancel one that is over — read from an injected clock so a test can move time instead of waiting.
steps.follows: Requests exist; this is what resolves them. The injected clock is what every time rule is tested through.

story.want: confirm and cancel bookings with the rules about time already passed
story.so: nobody cancels a slot that has already started and expects it back

steps.summary: Confirm and cancel are real transitions with rules that depend on the injected clock.

codes: the interval has begun; it can no longer be confirmed or moved
a cancelled booking cannot be confirmed or moved; request a new one
no such booking at this venue
cancelled; `late` is true when the interval had begun
the interval has ended; it can no longer be cancelled
no such booking at this venue

data: bookings gains confirmed_at, cancelled_at, late_cancel bool
rules: Confirm requires state requested and now < from. Cancel requires state requested or confirmed and now < to; if now ≥ from it is a late cancel — allowed and flagged `late`; the remainder of the slot is free from now, and since nobody can book the past nothing else needs protecting.
All `now` comparisons use the injected clock.
`Depends(get_clock)` overridable in tests.
Both the database session and the clock are `Depends` dependencies, so a test overrides either without touching the route.
ac_user: a club cancels a slot that started twenty minutes ago
it is marked cancelled late — the strip does not show the hour as free
Sabu confirms a slot that has begun
done: Both transitions with all refusals under a fixed clock; late flag stored.

try.do: Request a slot on the Book screen and open its booking card (the booking number in the green panel, or its block on The day). Press Confirm, then Confirm again. Request another slot, open it and press Cancel.
try.see: Confirm answers 200 with `confirmed_at`; a second Confirm is 409 already-confirmed. Cancel before the start answers `late: false`, and the block on The day turns grey. Once the interval has begun, Confirm is 409 already-started and Cancel is 200 with `late: true` — the card says "cancelled late" and the strip keeps the block, shown as cancelled, rather than showing the hour as free. After the interval has ended Cancel is 409 already-over. Every `now` is the injected clock (tests/test_transitions.py moves it, since the page runs on today's time).

steps.title: The refusals, once the shadows are counted
steps.scene: Two clubs are on the planner back to back at four o'clock. On paper they do not overlap. In reality one is clearing the ground while the other is putting up nets on it. And a booking a club cancelled last week must not come back just because someone presses confirm.
steps.build: Refuse an overlap once buffers are counted on both sides, and refuse a cancelled booking being reconfirmed — each with its own code, raised from a service function rather than a route.
steps.follows: The happy path is built. The buffered overlap is the whole point of this project, and it becomes the first row of its rule table.

story.want: be refused an overlap once buffers are counted on both sides
story.so: two clubs never arrive at the same ground on the same afternoon

steps.summary: Overlap is refused once buffers are counted on both sides, and a cancelled booking cannot be reconfirmed — each with its own code, raised from the service.

codes: the shadow (interval plus buffers) clashes with another booking's shadow; `clashes_with` lists booking ids and their held ranges
the shadow clashes with nothing live on that ground
a cancelled booking cannot be confirmed or moved; request a new one
the shadow (interval plus buffers) clashes with another booking's shadow; `clashes_with` lists booking ids and their held ranges

rules: Live bookings are requested (not past hold_until) and confirmed. A new request clashes if its shadow intersects any live booking's shadow on the same ground: `held_from_new < held_to_other AND held_from_other < held_to_new`.
Confirm re-runs the check (a competing request may have been confirmed since).
Domain refusals are exceptions (Overlap, Cancelled, AlreadyStarted, AlreadyOver) raised in the service and mapped by one handler.
The exception → status mapping lives in one `exception_handler` registration; routes never build error responses.
ac_user: refused: on paper they do not overlap, with buffers they do — and she is told which booking
ac_api: request 17:10–19:00 held from 16:30, exactly where A's shadow ends (half-open: touching shadows do not clash)
type, title, status, detail, named fields; no trace
done: Overlap on shadows both sides; reconfirm refused; one handler; a test per refusal.

try.do: Request ground A, League match, From 14:00, To 16:00 on a Saturday. Then request the same ground and day From 16:00, To 18:00. Then From 17:10, To 19:00. Cancel a booking on its card and press Confirm on it.
try.see: On paper 14:00-16:00 and 16:00-18:00 do not touch; with buffers the first is held to 16:30 and the second from 15:20, so the second is 409 overlap with `clashes_with` naming the first booking and its held range — The day marks the two shadows in red and draws the refused request hatched. 17:10-19:00 is held from 16:30 exactly and is 201: the predicate is half-open. Confirming a cancelled booking is 409 cancelled. Every refusal is raised in the service and mapped by the one handler in handlers.py; the table under the form lists each one the API documents.

steps.title: Moving a booking without breaking the day
steps.scene: Rafi asks to shift Saturday an hour later. Sabu erases the pencil mark, redraws it, and only then notices the school sports day.
steps.build: A move that re-checks the whole interval — including both buffers — in one transaction, so a booking is never briefly in two places or briefly in none.
steps.follows: What may not overlap is settled; a move is the first operation that could break it in the middle of itself.

story.want: move my booking and have the whole interval re-checked
story.so: a change of time cannot quietly create a clash

steps.summary: A move re-checks the whole new interval including both buffers, in one transaction — never briefly in two places or none.

try.do: Open a booking card (click its block on The day), then use the Move form on the card: first into a clash with the next booking on that ground, then into a free hour.
try.see: Into a clash: 409 overlap, and the block is still where it was — nothing was erased first. Into free time: 200 with the new held range, the block in its new place and the old interval free (the check excluded the booking itself, or every move would refuse itself). A failure injected after the check leaves the row untouched (tests/test_moves.py: the UPDATE and the event roll back together).

steps.title: A planner nobody can erase
steps.scene: Two clubs arrive at the same ground. The planner shows one booking, cleanly written, and nobody can say what was rubbed out.
steps.build: An append-only log: one row per transition — requested, confirmed, moved, cancelled — written in the same transaction as the change, never updated and never deleted.
steps.follows: A move rewrites history; this is what stops it being rewritten silently, and the log that proves nothing overlapped.

story.want: see every request, confirmation, move and cancellation in a record nobody can erase
story.so: a disputed Saturday has one account of what happened

steps.summary: Every transition is written to an append-only log in the same transaction, readable per booking.

codes: no such booking at this venue

data: events(id, venue_id, booking_id, kind requested|confirmed|moved|cancelled|expired|charged|invoiced|rechecked, at, actor_id, data json) — insert only; immutability enforced and tested
rules: Written in the same transaction; a rolled-back move leaves no `moved` event.
Events carry ids, intervals and facts — never the club's name, phone or email.
The booking's `events` are the only history shown.
Event rows are inserted with a plain INSERT in the same session transaction as the change; the events model has no update path.

he sees exactly what was requested, moved and confirmed, and when — nothing rubbed out

try.do: Open a booking you requested, confirmed, moved and cancelled.
try.see: The timeline: requested (with the interval), confirmed, moved (old and new intervals), cancelled (late or not) — each written in the same transaction as its change, in `at` order. Nothing can be edited: the database refuses UPDATE and DELETE on events (triggers, tested). No event carries the club, only ids, intervals and facts.

steps.title: The rule table, and then the rule changes
steps.scene: The city decides buffers should differ by event type: twenty minutes for a practice session, two hours for a sports day.
steps.build: A parametrised table of every refusal the planner can give, run through the test client with the clock overridden — then change the buffers (a uniform 40/30 table against each event type's own) and watch which rows move.
steps.follows: The refusals exist and time can be moved, so the buffer rule can be changed with evidence rather than hope.

story.want: set buffers per event type and see exactly which rules moved
story.so: a policy change does not quietly permit a clash

steps.summary: A parametrised rule table covers every refusal, then the buffers change - a uniform table against each type's own - and only the buffer rows move.
data: event_types.setup_minutes/teardown_minutes are the source of every buffer (loaded with the seed); the table also runs against a uniform 40/30 table, and there is no uniform-buffer setting
rules: The table: one row per case — ok / to before from / outside hours / shadow outside hours / overlap on the left buffer / overlap on the right buffer / back-to-back with buffers that just fit / confirm started / cancel over / late cancel / reconfirm cancelled / move into clash / move ok.
`pytest.mark.parametrize` from a CSV with the buffers as columns; clock via `dependency_overrides`.
Changing practice to 20/20 and school_day to 120/120 moves exactly the rows tagged `buffer`.
The table is one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `TestClient` with `dependency_overrides` for the clock; the rule change is a settings override in the same test module.

20 minutes is enough; a sports day would need two hours

steps.title: It survives being switched off

steps.follows: The image ran once; this makes it something the municipal office can be handed.
